This miscellaneous criminal case has been filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of charge-sheet lodged against the petitioners vide Crime No.73 of 2022 for offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 498- A, 323,34 of the Indian Penal Code and also under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 registered at Police Station-Mahila Thana NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:16204 2 MCRC-15478-2024 Bhopal, District-Bhopal (M.P.) and also challenges the order dated 03.10.2023 passed by the Court of Xth Additional Sessions Judge Bhopal,
District-Bhopal(M.P.) in S.T. No.805 of 2022 and also seeking quashment of all consequential proceedings arising therefrom.
2.
According to the case of the prosecution, the alleged incident took place during the period from 11.06.2017 to 29.03.2022.
An F.I.R. was lodged on 29.03.2022 stating that the petitioner and the prosecutrix were in a love affair for a long time, during which physical relations were established between them.

As a result, the prosecutrix became pregnant; however, she subsequently terminated Prakash Devani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84036402/
1 the pregnancy.

sentences.text: It is further alleged that when the petitioner refused to marry the prosecutrix, she lodged a complaint at Police Station Kolar.
Upon such complaint, the petitioner and his father assured the prosecutrix before the police authorities that the petitioner would marry her.
In view of this assurance, no offence was registered against him at that time.
Thereafter, on 14.07.2021, their marriage was solemnized at Arya Samaj Mandir, Nehru Nagar, Bhopal.

According to the prosecutrix, immediately after the marriage, the petitioner and his family members began harassing and humiliating her in connection with demand for dowry and subjected her to cruelty.
With these allegations offences as aforementioned have been registered against the petitioner and another co-accused person and criminal law is set in motion.

3 . Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in the instant case, parties have compromised the matter and the same has been duly verified by the Registrar-J(II).So far as Section 376 of IPC is concerned
